*Pre-Assignment*
Load all necessary packages, read in the clinical data.csv file you have in your analysis_data folder, and instantiate the MAF_object.
```{r}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath("/home1/kathlynp/490_cluster/analysis_data"))
options(timeout = 3600)

library(maftools)
library(TCGAbiolinks)
library(ggplot2)
figure_dir <- "/home1/kathlynp/490_cluster/week6_genomics/figures"
dir.create(figure_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

clin_path <- "/home1/kathlynp/GDCdata/TCGA-BRCA/Clinical/Clinical_Supplement/8162d394-8b64-4da2-9f5b-d164c54b9608/nationwidechildrens.org_clinical_patient_brca.txt"

clinical <- read.delim(clin_path,
                       na.strings = c("[Not Available]", "[Not Applicable]",
                                      "[Unknown]", "[Not Evaluated]",
                                      "[Discrepancy]", "[Completed]", ""),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Rows 1-2 are TCGA descriptor rows, not patients
clinical <- clinical[-c(1, 2), ]


# read.maf needs this column name to match clinical rows to samples
clinical$Tumor_Sample_Barcode <- clinical$bcr_patient_barcode

write.csv(clinical,
          "/home1/kathlynp/490_cluster/analysis_data/brca_clinical_data.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)

dim(clinical)
head(clinical$Tumor_Sample_Barcode)

clinic <- clinical

rds_path <- "/home1/kathlynp/490_cluster/analysis_data/maf_object.rds"

if (file.exists(rds_path)) {
  MAF_object <- readRDS(rds_path)
} else {
  maf_query <- GDCquery(
    project = "TCGA-BRCA",
    data.category = "Simple Nucleotide Variation",
    access = "open",
    data.type = "Masked Somatic Mutation",
    workflow.type = "Aliquot Ensemble Somatic Variant Merging and Masking"
  )

  GDCdownload(maf_query, method = "api", files.per.chunk = 100,
              directory = "/home1/kathlynp/GDCdata")

  maf <- GDCprepare(maf_query, directory = "/home1/kathlynp/GDCdata")

  MAF_object <- read.maf(maf = maf,
                         clinicalData = clinical,
                         isTCGA = TRUE)
}

MAF_object
```

It's useful to save your MAF_object, so that you don't have to go through the trouble of querying and preparing it everytime. The saveRDS function allows us to save an R object, allowing us to access it directly from our files. 
```{r}
saveRDS(
  MAF_object,
  file = "/home1/kathlynp/490_cluster/analysis_data/maf_object.rds"
)
```

When you reopen a new R session and want to access your MAF_object, you can use the readRDS function to load the object back into a new variable.
```{r}
MAF_object <- readRDS(file = "/home1/kathlynp/490_cluster/analysis_data/maf_object.rds")

MAF_object
```

*1*
Choose a clinical variable (or any variable from clin_rad or clin_drug) to separate your populations into two different groups and rewrite the column or create a new column with that variable as a factor. ***Do not use age or vital_status as your clinical variable.*** Hint: if your variable is continuous, you will need to determine your own cutoffs for the different levels of the factor. If your variable is categorical and has more than two possible values, choose the two that are the most common.
```{r}
node_col <- grep("lymph.*node.*examined|node.*examined",
                 colnames(clinic), value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)[1]
node_col

clinic$lymph_nodes_numeric <- suppressWarnings(
  as.numeric(as.character(clinic[[node_col]]))
)

median_nodes <- median(clinic$lymph_nodes_numeric, na.rm = TRUE)
median_nodes

clinic$node_group <- factor(
  ifelse(is.na(clinic$lymph_nodes_numeric), NA,
         ifelse(clinic$lymph_nodes_numeric <= median_nodes,
                "Lower Node Count", "Higher Node Count")),
  levels = c("Lower Node Count", "Higher Node Count")
)

table(clinic$node_group, useNA = "ifany")

clinic$patient_id <- substr(clinic$Tumor_Sample_Barcode, 1, 12)

samples <- getSampleSummary(MAF_object)$Tumor_Sample_Barcode


sample_clinic <- merge(
  data.frame(Tumor_Sample_Barcode = samples,
             patient_id = substr(samples, 1, 12)),
  clinic[!duplicated(clinic$patient_id),
         setdiff(names(clinic), "Tumor_Sample_Barcode")],
  by = "patient_id"
)

sample_clinic <- sample_clinic[!is.na(sample_clinic$node_group), ]

table(sample_clinic$node_group)
# For my clinical variable, I chose the number of lymph nodes examined. I then used the median to divide patients into those with a lower or equal number of nodes examined and those with a higher number.
```


*2*
Create a co-oncoplot with the top 10-20 (you choose) most mutated genes for the two groups. Pick one that has a large discrepancy in % mutated or type of mutations between the groups and research it. 
Research it. What is the gene used for? Can you think of any reason for the discrepancy?
```{r}
# How many usable numbers does each "node" column have?
node_cols <- grep("node", colnames(clinic), value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
counts <- sapply(node_cols, function(cn)
  sum(!is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(clinic[[cn]]))))))
counts

# Use the column with the most numbers
node_col <- names(which.max(counts))
node_col

clinic$lymph_nodes_numeric <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(clinic[[node_col]])))
median_nodes <- median(clinic$lymph_nodes_numeric, na.rm = TRUE)
median_nodes

clinic$node_group <- factor(
  ifelse(is.na(clinic$lymph_nodes_numeric), NA,
         ifelse(clinic$lymph_nodes_numeric <= median_nodes,
                "Lower Node Count", "Higher Node Count")),
  levels = c("Lower Node Count", "Higher Node Count"))

table(clinic$node_group, useNA = "ifany")
graphics.off()

maf_barcodes <- unique(as.character(MAF_object@data$Tumor_Sample_Barcode))
m <- regexpr("TCGA-[A-Za-z0-9]{2}-[A-Za-z0-9]{4}", maf_barcodes)
maf_ids <- ifelse(m > 0, substring(maf_barcodes, m, m + 11), NA)

head(maf_barcodes)
head(clinic$patient_id)
table(clinic$node_group, useNA = "ifany")
sum(maf_ids %in% clinic$patient_id)

lower_ids  <- clinic$patient_id[which(clinic$node_group == "Lower Node Count")]
higher_ids <- clinic$patient_id[which(clinic$node_group == "Higher Node Count")]

lower_samples  <- maf_barcodes[maf_ids %in% lower_ids]
higher_samples <- maf_barcodes[maf_ids %in% higher_ids]

length(lower_samples)
length(higher_samples)
stopifnot("lower_samples is empty: paste the output above" = length(lower_samples) > 0,
          "higher_samples is empty: paste the output above" = length(higher_samples) > 0)

sample_clinic <- data.frame(
  Tumor_Sample_Barcode = c(lower_samples, higher_samples),
  node_group = factor(c(rep("Lower Node Count", length(lower_samples)),
                        rep("Higher Node Count", length(higher_samples))),
                      levels = c("Lower Node Count", "Higher Node Count"))
)

maf_lower  <- subsetMaf(MAF_object, tsb = lower_samples,  mafObj = TRUE)
maf_higher <- subsetMaf(MAF_object, tsb = higher_samples, mafObj = TRUE)

# Co-oncoplot of the top 15 mutated genes
top_genes <- head(getGeneSummary(MAF_object)$Hugo_Symbol, 15)

pdf(file.path(figure_dir, "co_oncoplot_node_groups.pdf"), width = 14, height = 9)
coOncoplot(m1 = maf_lower, m2 = maf_higher,
           m1Name = "Lower Node Count", m2Name = "Higher Node Count",
           genes = top_genes)
dev.off()

gs_low  <- getGeneSummary(maf_lower)
gs_high <- getGeneSummary(maf_higher)
pct_low  <- 100 * gs_low$MutatedSamples[match(top_genes, gs_low$Hugo_Symbol)]   / length(lower_samples)
pct_high <- 100 * gs_high$MutatedSamples[match(top_genes, gs_high$Hugo_Symbol)] / length(higher_samples)
pct_low[is.na(pct_low)] <- 0
pct_high[is.na(pct_high)] <- 0

comparison <- data.frame(top_genes, pct_low, pct_high, diff = abs(pct_low - pct_high))
comparison <- comparison[order(-comparison$diff), ]
comparison

chosen_gene <- comparison$top_genes[1]
chosen_gene
```

# Q2 ANSWER: <what the gene does, and a possible reason for the difference between the groups>
# MAP3K1 gene is a kinase that helps control cell growth and death. This means that when it is mutated, it may cause breast cancer because the gene is turned off and cells won't die. A possible reason for the difference between groups may be because the MAP3K1 mutations are more common in the hormone receptor-positive tumors and not lymph nodes.

*3*
Create a contingency table with your variable and chosen gene. Run a Fisher’s Exact Test between presence of mutations for that gene and your clinical variable. Create and save a mosaic plot. 
Interpret the output of the Fisher’s Exact Test in terms of the odds ratio and p-value.
```{r}
graphics.off()

# samples with >= one mutation in the chosen gene
mutated_samples <- unique(as.character(
  MAF_object@data$Tumor_Sample_Barcode[MAF_object@data$Hugo_Symbol == chosen_gene]
))

sample_clinic$mutation_status <- factor(
  ifelse(as.character(sample_clinic$Tumor_Sample_Barcode) %in% mutated_samples,
         "Mutated", "Not Mutated"),
  levels = c("Mutated", "Not Mutated")
)

contingency_table <- table(sample_clinic$node_group, sample_clinic$mutation_status)
contingency_table

fisher_result <- fisher.test(contingency_table)
fisher_result
fisher_result$estimate
fisher_result$p.value

# mosaic plot
pdf(file.path(figure_dir, "mosaic_plot_mutation_status.pdf"), width = 8, height = 6)
mosaicplot(contingency_table,
           main = paste("Mutation Status of", chosen_gene),
           xlab = "Lymph Node Group", ylab = "Mutation Status",
           color = TRUE)
dev.off()
```

*5*
Create your Overall_Survival_Status column and create a mafSurvival KM plot based on mutations in your chosen gene.
Does there seem to be a difference? Hypothesize why or not based on the other analysis you did with the gene above.
```{r}
# Create survival status: 1 = dead, 0 = alive
clinic$Overall_Survival_Status <- ifelse(
  clinic$vital_status == "Dead", 1,
  ifelse(clinic$vital_status == "Alive", 0, NA)
)

# Convert survival time columns to numeric
death_days <- suppressWarnings(
  as.numeric(as.character(clinic$death_days_to))
)

followup_days <- suppressWarnings(
  as.numeric(as.character(clinic$last_contact_days_to))
)

# Calculate survival time
clinic$survival_time <- ifelse(
  clinic$Overall_Survival_Status == 1,
  death_days,
  followup_days
)

survival_data <- merge(
  data.frame(
    Tumor_Sample_Barcode = samples,
    patient_id = substr(samples, 1, 12)
  ),
  clinic[
    !duplicated(clinic$patient_id),
    c("patient_id", "survival_time",
      "Overall_Survival_Status")
  ],
  by = "patient_id"
)
survival_data <- survival_data[
  !is.na(survival_data$survival_time) &
  !is.na(survival_data$Overall_Survival_Status) &
  survival_data$survival_time >= 0,
]

# Kaplan-Meier plot
pdf(
  file.path(figure_dir, "kaplan_meier_gene_survival.pdf"),
  width = 9,
  height = 7
)

mafSurvival(
  maf = MAF_object,
  genes = chosen_gene,
  clinicalData = survival_data,
  time = "survival_time",
  Status = "Overall_Survival_Status"
)

dev.off()
# No, there doesn't seem to be a big differencein survival between the patients with and without a MAP3K1 mutation because p=0.809 and HR = 1.1. Although the mutant curve is lower after the 2000 day mark, only 82 patients are mutant compared to the 884 WT, so it's a small portion of patients that cause the drop. This suggests that it is probably not significant. A hypothesis on why this is happening is that MAP3K1 mutations are related with slower-growing tumors, as seen above, so the mutation itself is unlikely to change the patients overall survival. Also, the mutations are too spread out over the gene to tell
```
